text.p: BHF-Bank AG said on Wednesday it expected to post a satisfactory overall profit for 1997 after group pre-tax profit rose 10.4 percent to 181 million marks in the first six months.
"Building on the business revival in the first half we expect our commission business to remain positive," BHF said.
It added: "In view of moderate cost growth we are confident of being able to reach a satisfactory overall profit provided that markets remain good."

Administration costs rose 5.0 percent to 421 million marks. Own-account trading income fell 5.0 percent to 57 million marks but rose substantially if non-realised trading income is included, BHF-Bank said.
The balance sheet total rose to 79.7 billion marks at end-June from 74.1 billion at end-December. Lending rose 6.6 percent to 63.9 billion marks.

BHF, often touted as a prime takeover target, has emerged from a difficult 1996. Its operating profit fell five percent as earnings were hit by a dividend omission from industrial holding group AGIV AG, of which BHF owns just under 50 percent.
The bank said in its interim report that progress made in the restructuring of AGIV had led to the formation of substantial hidden reserves in its stake since the end of 1996.
Group operating profit after loan loss provisions rose 9.5 percent to 162 million marks in the first six months.
Net risk provisions rose 5.9 percent but the bank said it did not expect the need for provisioning to be as high in the full year 1997 as in 1996.

Earnings were driven by a 14.4 percent rise in commission income to 246 million marks amid booming stock markets while net interest income stagnated, rising 0.8 percent to 358 million marks, BHF said.
